q: What is the CBAM default value for Indian ferro-manganese, ferro-chrome and ferro-nickel?
title: CBAM default value: Indian ferro-alloys
short: For India: high-carbon ferro-manganese 1.690, low-carbon ferro-manganese 5.590, high-carbon ferro-chrome 2.350 and ferro-nickel 3.480 t CO2e per tonne. Low-carbon ferro-chrome shows no India value, so the table for other countries applies. Direct emissions only.
audience: Indian ferro-alloy producers in Odisha, Andhra Pradesh and elsewhere, and steelmakers buying from them

sections.h: India default values, t CO2e per tonne
ul: CN 7202 49 ferro-chromium, 4% carbon or less: no India value listed

sections.h: Where no India value is listed
p: When the India table shows a dash, the declarant uses the value for other countries and territories in the same annex, which is usually higher. A smelter in that position gains the most from measuring its own figure.
The listed values are increased by a mark-up: 10% for 2026, 20% for 2027 and 30% from 2028. Goods imported in 2026 always take the 2026 mark-up.

senseible: Senseible reads coal, coke, gas, electricity and freight invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so an actual figure you send an EU buyer can be traced back to the documents behind it. It does not file CBAM declarations.
